properties.decision:
The hub / project-brain thread is DEFERRED, deliberately and on Anthony's word, 2026-08-29. Nothing further is built — not the upward roll-up, not downward inheritance, not making Decision publishable, not the approver travelling in a surface.

**THE TRIGGER TO REVISIT IS NAMED AND IS A PERSON, NOT A DATE:** Alex, or another real user, saying they need it. Field demand, not a scheduled review.

HIS WORDS, and the two halves are separate claims: *"I think the value is obvious and we should do this. that being said, nobody is really asking for this at all and I'm hesitant to build it until Alex or someone else gives me feedback that they actually need it."*

⭐ SO THIS IS NOT A JUDGEMENT THAT THE FEATURE IS WRONG. He believes the value is obvious, from running programs where a sub-team not knowing a program decision has a cost he has watched. What is missing is DEMAND, and the two are different findings that a single "deferred" would have blurred.

TWO NEAR-MATCHES OFFERED AND BOTH READ. `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` is the QUESTION — what may cross a design boundary, and in which direction; this is the RULING ABOUT WHETHER TO ACT ON IT, and it deliberately leaves that question open rather than answering it. `fact:the-status-field-is-the-binding-versus-visible-switch` is the MEASUREMENT taken while investigating; it stands on its own whether or not anything is ever built. A parked question, a measurement, and a ruling not to proceed are three different states, and collapsing any two would either erase the thinking or claim it was concluded.

WHAT IS KEPT RATHER THAN DISCARDED — the thread produced real results and they stand whether or not the feature is ever built:
- Binding versus visible needs NO new mechanism: it is `accepted` versus `proposed`, and only the binding form needs the approver to travel. Measured against the real gate.
- The approver-loss defect prediction, with its bound corrected: that gate is reflow2-only and does not ship to consumers.
- The question, the upward form and the custody problem, all parked against this ruling rather than deleted.

📌 THE PREREQUISITE STAYS TRUE WHILE THIS IS PARKED: the hxm_program report measured ZERO of seven sibling designs exporting anything. Even a keen user cannot use a hub until something publishes. If demand arrives, the first work is getting one sibling to export — not the hub vocabulary.
properties.name: The hub is not built until a user asks for it — the value is not in doubt, the demand is
properties.rationale:
RECORDED BECAUSE RESTRAINT IS THE HARDEST THING FOR A DESIGN GRAPH TO HOLD. An idea that was built leaves a diff; an idea deliberately NOT built leaves nothing, and the next session finds four rich brainstorm nodes with an obvious next step and starts work. This is the node that stops that, and it names the condition under which starting would be right.

⭐ THE EVIDENCE THAT SUPPORTS THE RESTRAINT, measured rather than felt: the linking layer this feature would extend — `mirror_surface`, `export_surface`, `pair_designs`, `seam_report` — is BUILT, VERIFIED, and has ZERO INSTANCES in any real graph. `cap:built-and-consumed-by-nothing` is a detector this project wrote for exactly that shape. Building more of a layer nobody has used once is the failure mode Anthony names from acquisitions: *"designs get so overcomplicated when often a simple solution will do — engineers often over design something, it is kind of their nature."*

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT, stated so a later reader can overturn this properly: waiting for demand systematically underweights features whose value is invisible until they exist. Nobody asks for a thing they have not seen, and a program lead who has never had cross-project decision inheritance has no vocabulary to request it. That is a real cost of this ruling, and if it is ever overturned that is likely to be the reason.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT CHEAP TO REVISIT: the twenty-minute test that was NOT run — take one real program-level decision, put it in front of the person working that sub-project, and ask whether having it in their design would have changed what they did. It needs no code, it answers the demand question directly, and it stays available.
